overview: Explanatory sequential mixed methods study. Strand 1: a record-based cohort of OPAT episodes from 2021 to 2025 linked to emergency visits and vascular access records, and to agency visit notes if the agency agrees. Strand 2: semi-structured interviews with patients, carers and agency nurses sampled from the high- and low-complication groups found in strand 1. Integration by a joint display that sets each quantitative finding beside the explanations from the interviews.
population: Strand 1: all adults with an OPAT episode through a PICC or midline between January 2021 and December 2025 (about 1,870 episodes). Strand 2: about 16 patients or carers and 12 agency nurses.
exposure: Line type and lumens, antibiotic (vancomycin and vesicants flagged), planned course length, agency team, visit frequency, living alone and interpreter need.
procedures: The fellow links the OPAT database, emergency visit records and vascular access records by hospital number and codes complications with a written definition (occlusion, thrombosis, line-associated bloodstream infection, dislodgement, other). If the agency shares visit notes, home-managed complications are added and reported separately. Interview participants are sampled from agency teams and patient groups with the highest and lowest complication rates, with living alone and limited English deliberately included; interviews use a topic guide on line care, warning signs and escalation.

outcomes.name: Line complication with unplanned hospital contact or premature removal
outcomes.measure: Rate per 1,000 catheter days, coded from linked records with a written definition
outcomes.why: The event that interrupts treatment and brings patients back.

outcomes.name: Line-associated bloodstream infection
outcomes.measure: Positive blood culture attributed to the line by the infectious diseases team

outcomes.name: Explanations of how problems start, are noticed and are escalated
outcomes.measure: Themes from framework analysis of interviews
outcomes.why: Explains what the records cannot show.

outcomes.name: Completeness of complication capture
outcomes.measure: Proportion of complications found only in agency notes, if shared
outcomes.why: Shows how much a hospital-only count misses.

feasibility: Linkage and coding take about 35 fellow hours; about 28 interviews of 45 minutes take the remaining 25 hours with transcription paid from the service budget.
biasMitigation: Written complication definition applied before looking at exposures
Second coder for a random 10 percent of episodes
Adjustment for antibiotic, duration and indication when comparing line types
Interview sampling from both extremes, including patients living alone and with limited English
Home-managed events reported separately so the hospital-only count is not hidden

biasFlags.label: Missing home-managed complications
biasFlags.note: Depends on the agency gate; the undercount is stated if notes are not shared.

biasFlags.label: Confounding by line choice
biasFlags.note: Line type treated as a secondary contrast with adjustment.

biasFlags.label: Selection of interview participants
biasFlags.note: Extreme-case sampling explains variation, not typical experience.

flags: One quantitative primary outcome and one qualitative strand outcome
parsimony.simplestPath: One linked cohort, one primary rate, about 28 interviews and one joint display.

theoreticalFramework: Explanatory sequential mixed methods with a joint display for integration; SEIPS used only to organise interview findings into person, task, tool and organisation factors.
summary: Linked cohort followed by targeted interviews; one primary outcome; the agency notes decide how complete the count is.
